propositions: The test assertion uses bare substring containment (`"pandoc.org" in text`) which accepts lookalike hosts such as `https://pandoc.org.evil.com` (suffix) and `https://notpandoc.org` (prefix), failing to validate that NOTICE actionably points to upstream.
GitHub code-scanning alert #88 (`py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization`) flags the upstream-URL assertion as vulnerable to lookalike-host acceptance.

The fix replaces bare substring checks with a scheme+host-anchored regex using negative lookahead (`(?![\w.-])` and `(?![\w-])`) to reject both prefix- and suffix-style lookalikes while accepting valid URLs.

The anchored regex must accept `https://pandoc.org`, `https://www.pandoc.org`, `https://pandoc.org/`, and `https://github.com/jgm/pandoc` while rejecting `https://pandoc.org.evil.com`, `https://notpandoc.org`, and similar malformed variants.
After fix deployment and CodeQL re-analysis, alert #88 must transition from open to fixed state without manual dismissal.
